To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the client view should be taught first, and that the implementer view should be taught only after the client view.

(a) when teaching recursion, the client view should be emphasized over the implementer view; (b) when teaching recursion with a functional programming language (FPL), the FPL should be emphasized over imperative programming constructs (IPC) such as loops and assignment; and (c) the use of FPLs for teaching recursion can be a double-edged sword, because it can be used to support the client view, but also to blur the distinction between client and implementer views.
(1) the traditional teaching of recursion is biased toward the implementer view and (2) this bias leads to a less effective mental model for recursion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the teaching of recursion, but more generally, it aims to improve the teaching of programming language features and techniques that have a client-implementer dichotomy.
teaching programming language features that are often introduced in a way that does not respect client view first.
improving the quality of the mental models that students create when learning to program.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the client-view-first approach is the best way to teach recursion.
the client view should be the first view, not just for certain CS topics but for all programming language features.
the client view should be first in teaching programming language features and techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the client view is the most important perspective to convey to students, and the implementer view should be introduced only when the student is ready for it.
we are trying to help CS educators and students to think more clearly about the distinction between the implementer view and the client view.
we are arguing for the need for a more client-oriented approach to teaching recursion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the teaching of recursion can be significantly improved by adopting a client view first approach, and that the same approach can be used for other programming language features and programming techniques.
instructors should take a client view first approach to the teaching of programming language features and associated techniques.
the client view should come first, even when teaching programming language features.
